forge watch

Drop a folder, convert it, and Forge keeps watching it: every image you add afterwards is converted too, until you press ↵. Built around your portfolio’s public/images. Round eight: your picks only (the card D1 with the name in its edge, T1, R1, M2, today’s Save as).

Questions for you

  1. The card: D1 with FOLDER – images in the top edge (FOLDER in the mode’s colour, the dash grey, the name bold), and inside only “24 images · 86.4 MB”. A long name is cut in the middle so the edge keeps a little line after it: try name: long. Is this what you meant?
  2. Dropping the same folder again: with Same location, hero.webp from last time sits beside hero.jpg. Converting again would make hero (1).webp. Should Forge skip an image whose output is already there? I’d skip, and count it as left alone with “already converted”.
  3. Strings to approve (inside the screens): “↑ 1 failed” over the list when a failure has scrolled off the top; “↓ 1 new” when you have scrolled up and a file lands below; the key ↑↓ scroll once the list is longer than the room.
  4. Mixed folders (M2) strings: the title “Each kind”, “– not yet supported”, “– a text file”, and the keys ↵ change and s start. A kind’s answer reads like the bar’s trail: “WebP · 80”, “PNG · 150 dpi”.
  5. Changing a kind: the window, centred. Two strings to approve: its title (“3 PDFs”) and the key ←→ change; ↑↓ choose, ↵ done and esc cancel are the Mode window’s.
  6. An empty folder: today Forge refuses it (“holds nothing”). It could go straight to watching instead. Should it?
  7. Still open: a /watch command; remembering a folder’s settings; the reasons “not an image”, “already WebP”.

SCREENS · the same feature without the app

RULES · what it does when nobody is looking

  1. Dropping a folder always ends watching it; ↵ on Done stops. Converting a folder once is just: drop, convert, ↵.
  2. Output goes where Save as says, as today: Same location puts each WebP beside its original, in the watched folder. Forge never converts a file it wrote itself, so its own output is never picked up again.
  3. A file is read only once it has stopped growing (no change for 1 s): a screenshot being written, a copy or a download is never read half-done. .crdownload, .part, .download and hidden files are ignored.
  4. Probed by content, never by extension. What can’t become the chosen format is left alone and listed with why; nothing is touched that wasn’t converted. Originals are never changed.
  5. Name taken: keeps both (hero (1).webp). Nobody is there to ask.
  6. Writes are atomic (temp file, then rename), so a dev server watching the folder never sees half a WebP.
  7. Up to 4 files at a time. Each running file has its own row and true phase; never a percentage.
  8. Only while it runs: ↵, ctrl-c or closing the terminal stops it. Files that landed while the Mac slept are picked up on wake.
